Subject: Production slowdown after model upgrade — urgent

Tessa / team,

We pushed the new model bundle and quant profile (v2.3-q) to production at 02:00 UTC this morning and immediately saw a spike in request latency and an uptick in errors. Quick numbers from our dashboard: p95 ~ 1.1s -> 1.8s, p99 ~ 0.6s -> 2.4s, error rate from 0.2% -> ~3.8% (5xxs and timeouts). Throughput for our primary route dropped ~20% during the spike. This is impacting user flows (some payments calls are timing out).

I attached a sample perf dump and a few example request ids we captured. Can Redwood triage and either recommend a mitigation or roll us back to the previous profile ASAP? We're flagged at the exec level.

Sample request ids attached and in the perf dump.

— Raj

Quick triage notes (initial):
- I pulled the trace from the perf dump and correlated with infra metrics. Attached a short trace snippet (trace_snippet.txt).
- Observed: quantization profile v2.3 is invoking a fallback codepath on our current A100 fleet for some attention kernels. That fallback increases per-token kernel latency by ~3–4x for the affected sequence lengths (~384).
- Error spike appears tied to request-level timeouts (client 30s) after queued retries — not application-level model correctness.

Immediate mitigations we can do now:
1) Roll back to quant profile v2.2 for Velocity Labs (fastest).
2) Route traffic to a compatible model variant (v2.3-nq) that preserves previous kernels (requires config change but no rollback).

If Velocity wants rollback, we can schedule a short change window (5–10 minutes) — I'll need a confirmed time.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
SRE, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Production slowdown after model upgrade — urgent

Thanks Rishi — I dug into the kernel timing and pulled the compilation traces. Short summary: the quant changes in v2.3 change ordering of matmul kernels for sequences in your heat map, which on our A100 kernel combo causes an uncommon memory copy path. The result: some requests pay a ~1.6–2.8x CPU/GPU scheduling penalty.

Options (tradeoffs):
- Emergency rollback (v2.2): fastest restoration of prior p99/throughput. Minor risk: we lose the quality/size improvements from v2.3 for a short window.
- Patch forward: change the compiler kernel selection to force the prior kernel combination for affected lengths; requires a canary and ~6–12 hour validation, but preserves v2.3 improvements.

Given the customer impact (payments timeouts), my recommendation is rollback now and follow with a targeted patch. I've started an RFC + RCA draft and created Jira INF-983 (link above). Draft attached (rca_draft.docx).

— Markus
